brief: Deutsche Bank's positioning and flows update argues the Tech rotation it called in late July (the 5th in 2 years) is advanced but still has room to run: MCG & Tech is up 14% to a record high while the rest of the S&P 500 is down 3% since, having sold off 5.5% over 5 weeks. Tech positioning has risen to the 80th percentile but stays well below June's 99th-percentile peak. Aggregate equity positioning is overweight but not elevated, split between systematic strategies near a cycle high (89-91st percentile, vulnerable to vol shocks) and discretionary investors only moderately overweight because rising rates volatility, not its level, is capping exposure. CTAs added equity exposure across regions while staying extremely short bonds and long the dollar; vol-control funds are near-maxed with limited room to add. Sector positioning favors Tech and Energy over cyclicals and defensives. Separately, weekly fund flows diverged: equity funds saw their first outflow in three months (EM-led) even as bond and money-market funds gained inflows. The note also restates DB's standing 2026 S&P 500 target of 8000.
